To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
muon pairs are produced directly in collisions of high-energy muons with atomic nuclei.

(i) the cross section for direct muon-pair production by high-energy muon is significantly higher than that obtained earlier, (ii) the transverse-momentum distributions of muons are different from those obtained earlier, and (iii) the fluxes of groups generated by this process are much higher than those calculated earlier.

the cross section for direct production of muon-antimuon pairs by ultrarelativistically moving muons in the field of nuclei is affected significantly by the nuclear and atomic (electron cloud) form factors and is much less than that calculated earlier without regard to the atomic form factor.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a study of the process μ+μ−→e+e− in a strong electromagnetic field.
the possibility of detecting cosmic-ray muons of energy 100 TeV or higher.
the production of muon-antimuon pairs by ultrarelativistically moving muons.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the process μ+ Z → μ + Z + μ ++ μ − is a promising candidate for the detection of cosmic muons in the energy range from 100 to 500 GeV.
the process under consideration is of little importance for the physics of cosmic-ray muon interactions with nuclei.
the flux of muons produced by the direct process μ+Z is negligible at depths greater than 1 km.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the process of direct muon-pair production by cosmic-ray muons is of no importance for the problem of the origin of cosmic rays.

the fluxes of muons with a transverse momentum exceeding 100 MeV/c and an energy of 10 TeV or more, generated by the process considered, are of the order of 10−4 per m2 per steradian per second at sea level and 10−5 per m2 per second at a depth of 1 km of water equivalent.
the cross section is not very high and the probability of the direct muon production is not high enough to make the process of interest for the muon astronomy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cross section for direct muon pair production in the Coulomb field of nuclei is much larger than the cross sections for other processes of direct production of muons.
the fluxes of groups with energies Eμ>10GeV are much lower than the estimates of earlier authors.
